title: Router with Closed-Set Guard and Fail-Closed
description: A route function classifies each message with a model call and checks the label against a closed set of known routes. It fails closed by sending unknown labels to a human queue instead of silently misclassifying.
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: The ROUTES dictionary maps three known labels (event, change, question) to their destinations: digest, digest (marked UPDATED), and FAQ queue.
The route function calls the model with CLASSIFY prompt, strips and lowercases the label, then checks if it is in ROUTES.
Lines 6-7 are the closed-set guard: if the label is not in ROUTES, it returns the unknown label with 'needs_human' destination, failing closed and making the failure loud.

steps.question: What destination does an 'announcement' label get, and why?
steps.answer: needs_human, because announcement is not in the ROUTES dictionary

steps.description: The loop iterates through MESSAGES, calls route for each, prints the label and destination, and collects messages destined for digest into for_digest list.

The output shows 5 messages classified: 2 events to digest, 1 change to digest (UPDATED), 1 question to FAQ queue, 1 announcement to needs_human. Of these, 3 of 5 go to the pipeline with 5 model calls.
